issue.title: Do not try to exclude a master node that never existed
issue.body:

body: https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/1986 brings some context on how this impacts ECK.

The things we would lose with such an API include:

- validating that you didn't make a mistake and exclude a nonexistent node.
- support for excluding nodes by node attributes, e.g. to exclude a whole rack at once.
We discussed this last week and think we should do it, just based on node name and node ID.
Hi @DaveCTurner I can take a look at this one.

issue.title: Voting config exclusions should work with absent nodes

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body: Voting config exclusions should work with absent nodes. For details, please see #47990.

body:
Hi @DaveCTurner ,

Sorry for the delay on this. I had created a PR based on my understanding.  

One thing I did notice though is that when we start to allow absent node names and ids, this by definition would also allow incorrect names and ids as per my understanding there's no way to differentiate between the cases. Please let me know if this is expected.

Thanks,
Zach

Thanks @zacharymorn, yes, as I [noted above](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/47990#issuecomment-541641740) with this change we necessarily lose the ability to check that the nodes we're excluding aren't merely incorrect.
